facts.basis: Amazon's 2025 net income of $77.7 billion (GAAP, its Q4 2025 results release, February 2026; the same figures in a press-release copy and an independent report), spread evenly over a 365-day year of 31,536,000 seconds
facts.rate: $77.7B ÷ 31,536,000 = $2,463.85 a second ≈ $2,464 (to the dollar, the write-up's one rounding, because the swap-in rule divides by it)
facts.pay: median full-time pay $1,251 a week (BLS Q2 2026); a year of it × 52 = $65,052; half a year $32,526 (6 months, exact)
facts.swap_in: 2,464 ÷ your weekly pay = weeks of your work per second of Amazon's profit (median: $2,464 ÷ $1,251 = 1.97 ≈ 2)
facts.stop: the counter stops on exactly $65,052 (k × 26.4026 = $65,052.07), so the final carries no '≈'
facts.assumptions: an average rate (profit is seasonal and lumpy); 'profit' = GAAP net income for the full year as Amazon reports it; the weeks are gross median pay, before tax
facts.verdict: A year of median pay: ≈ 26 seconds.

youtube.title_pick: How Long Would You Have to Work for 1 Second of Amazon's Profit?
youtube.description:
How long would you have to work for 1 second of Amazon's profit? About 2 weeks, at median full-time pay. Amazon kept $77.7 billion in 2025: about $2,464 a second. A year of median pay goes by in about 26 seconds.

The math, shown:
• Amazon's 2025 net income: $77.7 billion.
• ÷ 31,536,000 seconds in a year ≈ $2,464 a second.
• Median full-time pay is $1,251 a week (BLS): $2,464 ÷ $1,251 ≈ 2 weeks of work per second.
• 5 seconds: ≈ $12,319, ≈ 10 weeks of median pay.
• Half a year of median pay, $32,526: ≈ 13 seconds.
• A year of it, $1,251 × 52 = $65,052: ≈ 26 seconds.
• Yours: 2,464 ÷ your weekly pay = your weeks per second.

Follow for the math behind your money — shown, not hand-waved. @envelopemath

Animation and original sound: The Back of the Envelope. Profit: Amazon's net income for full-year 2025 (GAAP, as Amazon reports it), from its Q4 2025 results (February 2026), spread evenly over a 365-day year; profit is seasonal and lumpy, so this is the year's average rate. Pay: BLS median usual weekly earnings of full-time wage and salary workers, Q2 2026 (gross, before tax). Not financial advice. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon.
#Amazon #Profit #MoneyMath
